correctness.rationale: For each job assigned to i, p_j<=r*p_j/|S_j|; summation gives L_i<=r P_i at every prefix. In the adaptive r-ary tournament the last champion receives h jobs and belongs to h eligibility sets; therefore its unit-job Prop1 ratio is exactly r(1-1/h), tending to r. Each new hyperedge joins disjoint components, proving Berge acyclicity. Executed exact rational checks independently examine finite cases; no finite result is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Maximum number r of feasible recipients per job is a natural parameter in skill-eligibility and hypergraph orientation. The all-r exact minimax value is accompanied by a substantive acyclic counterexample: unit chores on a simple tree already force approaching factor two, even though offline Prop1 always exists. The theorem separates acyclicity from online proportionality and identifies a structural phase law rather than an arbitrary finite example.
